prompt: We don't do any design — customers hand us complete drawings. What does ISO 9001 require when we define the scope of our QMS and want to leave design out?
response:
When defining the scope of your Quality Management System (QMS) under ISO 9001, and you want to exclude the design process because customers provide you with complete drawings, you need to clearly document this exclusion. Here’s how you can approach it:

### 1. Define the Scope of Your QMS
The scope should clearly state the boundaries and applicability of your QMS. This includes specifying which processes are included and which are excluded.

### 2. Document the Exclusion
In the scope definition, explicitly state that the design process is excluded because it is provided by customers. 

### Example Scope Statement:
```
The scope of our Quality Management System (QMS) includes all processes related to the procurement, production, and delivery of products based on customer-provided complete drawings. The design process is excluded from the scope of this QMS, as design activities are fully handled by our customers who provide us with complete drawings.
```

### 3. Justify the Exclusion
You must provide a justification for excluding the design process. This is typically documented in your QMS documentation.

### Example Justification:
```
The design process is excluded from our QMS because:
- Customers provide us with complete and detailed drawings.
- Our role is to procure materials, produce, and deliver the product based on these provided drawings.
- We do not engage in any design activities.
```

### 4. Ensure Consistency with ISO 9001 Requirements
Even though design is excluded, ensure that all other relevant processes are covered by your QMS and meet the requirements of ISO 9001.

### 5. Communicate with Customers and Stakeholders
Make sure that customers and other relevant stakeholders are aware of the scope and exclusions of your QMS. This helps manage expectations and ensures clarity in your business relationships.

### 6. Maintain Documentation
Keep all scope definitions, exclusions, and justifications documented and readily available for review during internal audits and external certification audits.

By clearly defining and documenting the scope of your QMS and the exclusion of the design process, you can comply with ISO 9001 requirements while accurately reflecting your business operations.
